answer.rationale: memory_b1 verified: rollback cleared the checkout error spike; prior build was stable and finished without customer impact. Current state mirrors that precedent: release went out 2h ago, p99 write latency has been climbing for 90min (inside the release window), degradation is confined to the primary region, and settlement writes are at peak. A rollback restores the last-known-good build fast and stops the degradation at its likely source without moving traffic, so customer writes stay on the primary with no failover cutover risk. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the natural second-choice if latency does not recover within ~15 minutes of the rollback, but it carries more moving parts during peak writes. Adding capacity (memory_b3) does not address a likely regression, and routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) does not help the write path that is degrading. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against dependency outages, not a release-induced write-path slowdown. One intervention, highest expected value: rollback_release.
